meta.scope: Ecuador batch 2 — External sector (BOP, trade), oil vs non-oil export structure, reserves, producer prices, and dollarization context.

candidates.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
candidates.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
candidates.notes: Core external-accounts product. 2025 current-account surplus reached a historical high of ~USD 7.7 bn, driven by the goods surplus and secondary income (remittances).

candidates.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
candidates.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, with a sharp analytical split between oil and non-oil trade.
candidates.notes: Trade data feed the BOP and national accounts. Non-oil exports (shrimp, cocoa, banana, mining) have become the main growth engine; oil remains important but has lost relative weight.

candidates.title: Exportaciones e ingresos petroleros / Oil exports & fiscal contribution
candidates.description: Statistics of crude-oil and derivatives production, exports and related fiscal revenues. Historically the dominant export and a major source of public revenue.
candidates.notes: Structural but declining relative weight. 2025 oil exports ~USD 7.8 bn (down ~19% year-on-year). Still a key fiscal and external-sector variable, but non-oil exports now exceed oil by a wide margin.

candidates.title: Exportaciones no petroleras (camarón, cacao, banano, minería)
candidates.description: Non-oil merchandise exports, led by shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, banana/plantain and mining products. Principal recent driver of the trade surplus and of export diversification.
candidates.notes: 2025 non-oil exports ~USD 29.4 bn (+18%). Shrimp, cocoa and banana are the headline traditional non-oil lines; mining has also grown. Central to the narrative of export diversification under dollarization.

candidates.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco Central del Ecuador
candidates.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the central bank. Critical liquidity buffer in a fully dollarized economy.
candidates.notes: Key external-buffer indicator under dollarization. End-2025 reserves reached record levels (~USD 9.8 bn). Cover deposits of the financial system and provide confidence in the dollarized regime.

candidates.title: Régimen de dolarización oficial (desde 2000)
candidates.publisher: Banco Central del Ecuador / Marco legal
candidates.description: Official dollarization of the Ecuadorian economy (US dollar as legal tender since 2000). Defines the monetary regime: no independent national currency or classic policy interest rate.
referenced_by: Every major BCE macroeconomic and monetary report
Analysis of inflation, reserves and financial stability
candidates.notes: Foundational institutional regime node. Continuously cited as the framework that constrains monetary policy and elevates the importance of fiscal discipline, reserves and external competitiveness.

candidates.title: Índice Nacional de Precios al Productor (INPP)
candidates.description: Monthly producer price index, published with and without oil. Measures price changes at the producer level across agriculture, mining, manufacturing and utilities.
candidates.notes: Complements the IPC. The oil/non-oil split mirrors the trade and production analysis. Useful for cost-push and industrial-price monitoring.

candidates.title: Canasta Familiar Básica y Canasta Familiar Vital
candidates.description: Official cost of the basic and vital family baskets, published monthly with the IPC. Used for living-cost and wage-reference analysis.
candidates.notes: High-visibility living-cost indicator. Linked to the IPC and frequently cited in wage and social-policy discussion.

candidates.title: Remesas de trabajadores / Secondary income (remittances)
candidates.description: Statistics of worker remittances received from abroad. Major component of the secondary-income account and a stabilising factor in the balance of payments.
candidates.notes: Structurally important inflow. Contributed to the record current-account surplus in 2025. Complements the goods-trade surplus in the external accounts.

candidates.title: Camarón, cacao y banano — leading non-oil export products
candidates.description: Product-level export statistics for the three largest non-oil traditional export lines: shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, and banana/plantain.
candidates.notes: These three products dominate non-oil traditional exports. Shrimp has overtaken oil in some recent periods as the single largest export earner; cocoa has seen exceptional value growth.

proposed_edges.basis: Balance of payments is compiled by the Banco Central del Ecuador.
Merchandise trade flows are a primary input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
Oil is the historic core of merchandise exports (now declining in relative weight).
Non-oil exports are the growing majority of the export basket.
Changes in reserve assets appear in the balance of payments.
Dollarization is the monetary regime under which the BCE operates.
Shrimp, cocoa and banana are the leading non-oil traditional export products.
The basic and vital baskets are priced with the same price data underlying the IPC.
